title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.

providers.name: GitHub Enterprise Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Enterprise Cloud feature scope. Fine-grained PATs, classic PATs and GitHub Apps have different approval/revocation rules.

controls.name: IP allow list
controls.what: Blocks PATs, OAuth app tokens, SSH/deploy keys, GitHub App tokens and GITHUB_TOKEN from non-allowed IPs (not user-installed apps' installation tokens).
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security > IP allow list; Enterprise settings > Authentication security
controls.quote: IP allow lists don't currently restrict access when a GitHub App is installed on a user account and uses server-to-server installation tokens to access an organization or enterprise.

controls.name: Workflow permissions (default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions)
controls.what: Sets the default GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only contents/packages or read/write; workflows can still change it via the permissions key.
controls.setting: Org/Enterprise settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions
controls.quote: Under "Workflow permissions", choose whether you want the GITHUB_TOKEN to have read and write access for all permissions (the permissive setting), or just read access for the contents and packages permissions (the restricted setting).

controls.name: Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests
controls.what: When off, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot create or approve pull requests.
controls.setting: Org/Enterprise settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions
controls.quote: By default, when you create a new organization, workflows are not allowed to create or approve pull requests.

controls.name: Send write tokens to workflows from pull requests (fork PRs)
controls.what: Controls whether fork pull-request workflows get a write GITHUB_TOKEN; otherwise it is read-only.
controls.setting: Org/Enterprise settings > Actions > General > Fork pull request workflows
controls.quote: Run workflows from fork pull requests. Users can run workflows from fork pull requests. By default, workflows will use a GITHUB_TOKEN with read-only permission, with no access to secrets.

controls.name: Actions policies (disable GitHub Actions)
controls.what: Disabling Actions for all or selected repositories prevents workflows (and their GITHUB_TOKEN) from running.
controls.setting: Org settings > Actions > General > Policies; enterprise policy can override
controls.quote: You can choose to disable GitHub Actions for all repositories in your organization, or only allow specific repositories.

no_control.what: Admins cannot stop repo writers from raising GITHUB_TOKEN permissions in the workflow file above the default.
no_control.quote: Anyone with write access to a repository can modify the permissions granted to the GITHUB_TOKEN, adding or removing access as required, by editing the permissions key in the workflow file.

controls_unknown: Whether admins can set a maximum lifetime for GitHub App user access tokens or OAuth app tokens (only app-developer settings found).
Whether GITHUB_TOKEN workflow permission defaults can be made non-overridable.

authentication.summary: Classic/fine-grained PATs, OAuth app tokens, GitHub App installation/user tokens, and Actions GITHUB_TOKEN.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Allow list explicitly covers the Actions GITHUB_TOKEN. Jobs must run on self-hosted runners or GitHub-hosted larger runners with static IP ranges that are added to the list.

renewal.summary: The platform supplies a token for the workflow job.

administration.summary: Repository/permission-scoped apps and PATs; PAT approval/restriction and lifetime policy; SAML authorization; revoke tokens or suspend/uninstall apps.
administration.conditions: Enterprise Cloud feature scope. Fine-grained PATs, classic PATs and GitHub Apps have different approval/revocation rules.

sso.details: GITHUB_TOKEN is repository-scoped and marked as not supporting SSO authorization in the credential types table; SSO bulk actions do not affect it.

offboard.details: The token belongs to a workflow job and expires when the job ends.

expiry.ui: Not configurable: token expires when the job finishes (max 24 h refresh)

reads.ui: Enterprise Settings > Audit log > Export Git Events; filter JSON on action git.clone and repo

kill.ui: Repo > Actions > workflow > run > Cancel workflow

token_format.notes: GITHUB_TOKEN is a GitHub App installation token, so ghs_ (incl. new ghs_APPID_JWT). Expires at job end; max 6h hosted, refreshable to 24h self-hosted.

log_sources.name: GitHub organization/enterprise audit log
log_sources.notes: Records token-authenticated actions with hashed_token, programmatic_access_type, token_scopes. 180 days; Git events 7 days and only via REST include=git, streaming or export. IP disclosure is opt-in.

log_sources.name: Audit log streaming (enterprise)
log_sources.notes: Needed to keep Git events beyond 7 days; api.request events (enterprise setting, streaming only).

log_sources.name: Workflow run logs
log_sources.notes: Only step stdout; correlate with audit log.

credential_id_fields.notes: Common field; GITHUB_TOKEN-specific use not documented

lifecycle_events.notes: Job start; token minted; streaming/export/REST only
Run done; token expires at job end

default_workflow_permissions switched to write before a suspicious run

containment.steps: Cancel in-progress runs; disable Actions for repo/org; remove self-hosted runners; set default workflow permissions to read.
containment.notes: No manual revocation; token dies at job end. Not affected by enterprise bulk credential actions. Rotate any other secrets exposed to the job.

sample_query.purpose: List jobs (and secrets passed) in the incident window.

calls.log_notes: Reads not in standard audit log

calls.reveals: full history of the workflow's repository
calls.log_notes: Enterprise Cloud only; GITHUB_TOKEN scoped to the one repo

detections.title: GitHub Workflow Permissions Modified
detections.detects: Changes to the organization default GITHUB_TOKEN workflow permissions.

detections.title: GitHub Workflow Dispatched by GitHub Actions Bot
detections.detects: github-actions[bot] using a server-to-server token (GITHUB_TOKEN) to start a workflow via workflow_dispatch, a sign of a stolen GITHUB_TOKEN being replayed.
